blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized caregiver preparation for transition home after stroke
stem: A family caregiver will assist a client with residual deficits after stroke at home. Which teaching plan by the RN best reflects AHA/ASA caregiver-support guidance?

options.A: Assess the caregiver's needs, combine practical skill building with psychoeducation, and plan reassessment after discharge as needs change.
options.B: Provide the standard stroke education packet before discharge and arrange practical skills training after home services have begun.
options.C: Teach the required caregiving procedures before discharge and use the same psychoeducational content for caregivers with similar client deficits.
options.D: Focus on emotional support during hospitalization and postpone individualized skill building until the caregiver reports difficulty after discharge.

rationale: A is correct. The AHA/ASA adult stroke rehabilitation guideline recommends caregiver interventions that combine skill-building with psychoeducational strategies, are tailored to the individual caregiver's needs, and include postdischarge assessment with interventions adjusted as needs change. The 2026 AHA/ASA acute ischemic stroke guideline continues to list the adult stroke rehabilitation guideline as an associated guideline and directs readers to it for detailed postdischarge rehabilitation practice. B is incorrect because a standardized information-first approach defers needed practical skill preparation and is not individualized. C is incorrect because providing procedures does not substitute for tailoring the broader caregiver intervention to the caregiver's assessed needs. D is incorrect because psychoeducation/support without concurrent skill building is not the preferred approach, and individualized caregiver preparation should not be deferred until difficulty is reported after discharge.
educational_objective: Prepare stroke caregivers with needs-based interventions that combine practical skill building and psychoeducation, then reassess and tailor support after discharge as caregiver needs change.
source_document_title: Guidelines for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery; 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With Acute Ischemic Stroke
source_version_date: Adult stroke rehabilitation guideline originally published May 4, 2016 with 2017 correction/addendum; 2026 AIS guideline published January 26, 2026 and continues to list the 2016 rehabilitation guideline as associated poststroke rehabilitation guidance; sources rechecked 2026-08-20
source_locator: 2016 AHA/ASA Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery — Transitions in Care and Community Rehabilitation / family caregiver education and support: Class I recommendations state that interventions combining skill building with psychoeducational strategies should be chosen over psychoeducation alone; interventions should be tailored to individual caregiver needs rather than one-size-fits-all; postdischarge assessments with tailored interventions based on changing needs should be performed. 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline — Table of Associated AHA/ASA Guidelines and Statements lists Guidelines for Adult Stroke Rehabilitation and Recovery (2016); Section 5.7 Rehabilitation states that a detailed review of postdischarge rehabilitation practice is available in that guideline.
source_claim_supported: Stroke caregiver interventions should combine skill building and psychoeducation, be individualized to caregiver needs, and include postdischarge reassessment with support adjusted as needs change; the 2016 rehabilitation guideline remains an associated poststroke rehabilitation resource in the 2026 AHA/ASA AIS guideline.
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care, printed page 7/PDF page 11 and Appendix A Case Management: identify and collaborate with multidisciplinary team members; assess referral/resource needs; coordinate care across settings; provide individualized discharge information and preparation for transition to home/community.
pdf_visual_verification: NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan relevant Management of Care content was visually verified by screenshot earlier in this 2026-08-20 audit session. The AHA/ASA evidence used for this item was verified through current free-access HTML pages, so no AHA PDF is relied upon for the item.
targeted_near_duplicate_check: Repository-targeted search for 'stroke caregiver skill building psychoeducation individualized postdischarge assessment' returned no indexed matching files; no near-duplicate identified by the targeted check.
correction_summary: Retained the caregiver-support construct and rebuilt the alternatives to remove 'only/all' cueing and the uniquely longest key. The revised item tests three realistic errors: standardized information with delayed skills, procedure teaching without caregiver-level tailoring, and support-first care with delayed individualized skill building. Adversarial reread removed a residual 'only if' cue from D.

option_audit.A: Correct; directly integrates the three AHA/ASA-supported elements: skill building plus psychoeducation, individualized needs assessment, and postdischarge reassessment.
option_audit.B: Plausible information-first transition error; incorrect because it defers practical skill preparation and uses a standardized approach rather than needs-based intervention.
option_audit.C: Plausible task-training-only error; incorrect because caregiver interventions should be individualized beyond client-deficit similarity.
option_audit.D: Plausible emotional-support-first error; incorrect because preferred caregiver interventions combine psychoeducation/support with skill building rather than delaying skill building until problems arise.

cueing_audit.absolute_words: No option relies on always/never/only/all/must-type absolutes after adversarial correction.
cueing_audit.answer_length: Final alternatives are comparable in length and detail; the correct answer is not the uniquely longest option.
cueing_audit.grammatical_lexical: All four alternatives are parallel caregiver-teaching plans.
cueing_audit.second_answer_risk: No defensible second answer identified after AHA/ASA source-based reread.
